title: Minimax Private Estimation of Smooth Optimal-Transport Maps
topic: Social Aspects->Privacy-preserving Statistics and Machine Learning
claim: Estimation error falls with sample size and stronger privacy costs accuracy, with the private estimator approaching non-private baselines as data grows.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, log-log line plots, legends inside, shaded confidence bands
description: Two side-by-side log-log line plots, (a) d=2 and (b) d=3. Each plots mean squared error on the y-axis against sample size n on the x-axis, from about 250 to 16,000. Colored solid lines with circle markers and shaded bands show the wavelet estimator at different privacy budgets ε. Panel (a) uses ε = ∞, 10, 5 and 1. Panel (b) uses ε = ∞, 30, 10 and 5. Black dashed (OT) and red dashed (EOT) baseline lines run diagonally downward through the middle. Smaller ε curves sit higher and drop more steeply as n grows, converging toward the baselines at large n. In (b) the curves stay higher because of the higher dimension. Legends sit inside each panel. The eye goes first to the spread of colored curves and the baseline pair.
caption: unif-unif, N=2, J=2, for d=2 (a) and d=3 (b). Mean squared error vs. sample size $n$ for varying central privacy budgets $\epsilon$ (log-log scale), averaged over 5 independent runs. Solid lines represent the $\epsilon$-DP wavelet estimator; black and red dashed lines denote the OT and EOT baselines, respectively.
abstract: We study the problem of estimating smooth optimal transport (OT) maps between two probability distributions under differential privacy (DP) constraints. Leveraging wavelet-based density estimators and recent stability bounds for smooth OT maps, we propose differentially private estimators that apply to both central and local DP models. Our main estimator achieves near-minimax optimal rates in dimension $d \geq 2$, and we complement it with a quantile-based estimator that attains minimax optimal rates in dimension $d = 1$ under central DP. We further establish matching minimax lower bounds, confirming the near-optimality of our approach. To the best of our knowledge, this constitutes the first differentially private procedure for OT map estimation with minimax optimality guarantees.
